name: U.S. Naval Research Laboratory (NRL)
summary: Navy research facility that pioneered practical radar development in 1930s, achieved first aircraft detection by radio (1930), developed first operational pulse radar (1934), installed first US radar on USS New York (1938)

1922_discovery.observation: Ship crossing transmission path of radio link produced slow fading in and out of signal
1922_discovery.significance: First observation of radio detection principle

1930_aircraft_detection.achievement: Used radio equipment to detect passing aircraft
1930_aircraft_detection.significance: First practical demonstration of aircraft detection by radio

1934_breakthrough.achievement: Worked out practical technology for pulse radar
1934_breakthrough.significance: Beginning of effective radar program in United States
1934_breakthrough.december_1934: Breadboard apparatus successfully detected aircraft at range of one mile

congressional_funding.source: Committee on Naval Appropriations, US House of Representatives
congressional_funding.impact: Enabled transition from experimental to operational radar systems

first_operational_radar.significance: First US radar permanently installed on naval vessel
first_operational_radar.operational_status: Functional radar system for naval operations

research_period_1930_1940.focus: Use of radio for ranging and detection
achievements: 1938 - First operational deployment (XAF on USS New York)
research_period_1930_1940.impact: Established US as radar technology leader entering WWII

note_on_entity_name.clarification: Research was conducted at NRL, not a Naval Intelligence facility
note_on_entity_name.intelligence_connection: Radar intelligence applications developed, but institution was research-focused

significance: Pioneered US radar development, critical technology advantage in WWII, established foundation for modern electronic warfare and detection systems
research_quality: HIGH - Well-documented historical record, Engineering and Technology History Wiki, Naval History archives
